changes: No code changes — package.json deliberately NOT modified. Only CHANGELOG.md modified: Unreleased entry honestly documents Plan A as empirically falsified with outcome=blocked, cites concrete falsification data (3x N=4 runs, wall-clock 11-14min vs predicted 5-7, new race victims, cli-json-stdout-contract still timed out at 300s under N=4 — proving worker count is NOT the root cause), and points to Plan B (two-pass retry) as the follow-up.
usage: No user-facing change. Developers continue using npm run test:all as before (runner default, ~3min wall-clock with intermittent races). The deliverable is the falsification data in F-001 and the CHANGELOG entry: future engineers know that lowering --jobs is NOT the solution.
expectedOutcome: package.json test:all script unchanged from main; CHANGELOG Unreleased entry under Test infrastructure names B-be91 with outcome=blocked + the run data + Plan B pointer.
actualTranscript: 3x test:all --jobs 4 measurement: run 1 = 159/167 PASS exit 1 in 861s (8 timeouts incl. cli-json-stdout-contract@300s + 4 new victims), run 2 = 165/167 in 654s, run 3 truncated. Wall-clock at N=4 = 11-14min directly contradicts predicted 5-7min. Finding B-be91:F-001 (high) filed. 4 reviewer lanes PASS (concept RP-002, quality RP-001, test-coverage RP-003, docs RP-004). All 19 intents recorded with verdict=waived + literal intent commands per memory rule. Delivery review PASS 3/3 docsPromises + 3/3 features (all waived as honest negative result).
outcomeDiff: Outcome is BLOCKED, not delivered. Plan A hypothesis falsified by experiment — explicit difference vs PLAN-time expected 3-consecutive-green. This IS the correct outcome for a falsification-purpose story; the value is the data, not a script edit.
limitations: Plan A's core hypothesis (worker count is the root cause) is disproven. The parallel-race convergence-tail remains unresolved. test:all continues to have intermittent timeouts and one parallel-only FAIL (review-pass-discard). Plan B story (two-pass retry — pass 1 high-concurrency, pass 2 serial retry for timeouts) is the follow-up; it does NOT depend on N being correct since any race that resolves in single-process mode passes the retry.
pitfalls: (1) Plan A's hypothesis (8-worker kernel-resource contention) was plausible but empirically wrong — falsified by the SAME smoke (cli-json-stdout-contract) timing out at its 300s ceiling under N=4 just as under N=8. Lesson: when bumping per-smoke timeoutMs surfaces NEW victims (B-24c3 convergence-tail), the next hypothesis must distinguish between absolute-time, shared-state, and pool-size mechanisms. (2) Wall-clock at N=4 (11-14min) ballooned beyond predicted 5-7min because head-of-line blocking: slow smokes occupy worker slots while fast smokes queue. Lesson: lower N reduces concurrency but ALSO reduces throughput when slow tasks dominate. (3) Future Plan B design should NOT assume any N is correct — two-pass retry isolates rather than fixes the race.
